name: Hotel Cala di Volpe
insider_take: This legendary Costa Smeralda resort was designed to look like an ancient Mediterranean fishing village, complete with handcrafted architectural details that make it appear centuries old despite opening in 1963.
whats_special: Hotel Cala di Volpe was originally conceived by Prince Karim Aga Khan IV as part of his vision to transform Sardinia's northeast coast into a luxury destination. The hotel's unique design features no straight lines—every wall, window, and terrace curves organically like natural rock formations. It's also been a favorite filming location, most famously serving as James Bond's hotel in "The Spy Who Loved Me."
pro_tip: Book a harbor-view room to watch the parade of superyachts in Porto Cervo's marina, especially during the Maxi Yacht Rolex Cup in September when some of the world's most impressive sailing vessels compete right outside your window.
dont_miss: The hotel's private beach at Cala di Volpe bay offers some of the most pristine waters in the Mediterranean, while the nearby Porto Cervo marina is a prime spot for celebrity spotting during summer months. Take the scenic coastal drive to Capo Testa, where massive granite boulders create otherworldly landscapes that have been sculpted by wind and sea for millennia.
pros: Iconic Costa Smeralda location with pristine Mediterranean beaches
Legendary luxury resort featured in classic films and favored by celebrities
Authentic Sardinian architecture with stunning emerald coastline views
World-class spa and exclusive yacht club access
cons: Premium pricing reflective of ultra-luxury positioning
